key_insight: This paper shows that diffusion models for lattice field theories do not need real target samples to be trained. Instead, they can learn from their own generated samples, removing the main data requirement that made standard training impractical.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the bottleneck of generating equilibrium field configurations in lattice field theory, where obtaining true samples from the target distribution is computationally expensive and limits the use of standard diffusion-model training.
method: Train diffusion models using self-generated samples rather than requiring samples from the target lattice distribution.
Adapt the denoising score matching framework so it can operate in a data-free or self-referential setting.
Use the model as a generative sampler to produce independent field configurations for lattice field theory applications.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this removes a major barrier to applying diffusion models in scientific domains where labeled or target-distribution data are costly or unavailable. It opens the door to practical generative sampling workflows in physics and other simulation-heavy fields.

paper_title: Data Free Training of Diffusion Models for Lattice Field Theories
paper_authors: Dennis Grinwald, Ankur Singha, Khaled Kahouli, Karl Jansen, Shinichi Nakajima
